Numbered chapter 1:
[1] Cold woke him first, before memory did — a cold so total it seemed less a temperature than a subtraction, as though something essential had been drawn out of him and replaced with glass.
[2] He lay on his back in the white, and the sky above was a flat, colorless lid.
[3] His teeth ached.
[4] Behind his eyes a slow pulse beat, the afterimage of the jump, nausea rolling through him in thin waves.
[5] He pushed himself up on one elbow.
[6] The snow had begun to settle into the folds of his coat, into the seams, patient as a thief.
[7] He knew the arithmetic of this: skin to shivering, shivering to numbness, numbness to a sleep that did not end.
[8] Hours.
[9] Perhaps fewer.
[10] He got his knees under him.
[11] The wind came across the tundra without hurry, carrying grains of ice that stung his cheek, and he turned from it, scanning.
[12] A rise of dark rock to the west, low and broken, and beyond it a shadow that might have been a ravine.
[13] He had spent a lifetime learning to arrive.
[14] No one had taught him the first thing about surviving it.
[15] He started walking, counting his steps, because counting was something to do.
